notes.title: Hotfix #4
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with the Mushroom Eater ending: [spoiler] saving via Kombucha on days 7–10 before unlocking any ending, then completing a normal ending, would incorrectly unlock Mushroom Eater [/spoiler]. The game now properly tracks whether Mushroom Eater was unlocked at the start of the run

[/list]

notes.title: Hotfix #3
100k copies sold – What’s next?
notes.content:
[i]Knock-knock-knock[/i]. It’s us. Carrying a bag of improvements we’re set to deliver – based on your feedback! So let’s talk about them.

First, it was apparent that the [b]current save system might be too punishing[/b]. Sure, we’ve wanted for it to feel meaningful and scarce, but not punishing. At least not in a sense of punishing you for having a life outside of playing games. 

As such, we’re planning to introduce the [b]save on quit[/b] feature. It does exactly what you’d expect: automatically saving your game when you decide it’s enough anxiety and dread for today, and press Quit. [b]The save is going to be rewritten each time you quit, though[/b], and isn’t accessible outside of pressing the “Continue” button. Also, keep in mind that [b]quitting via Alt+F4 doesn’t save the game, and you won’t be able to save via this feature on the final day of any ending[/b]. On the plus side though, [b]your manual saves will stay after the game’s completion[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/ea13932ad919f3aca2c4ddcce51959539342334a.gif[/img]

Speaking of! [b]The Neighbour[/b]. He’s a nice guy, sure, but why do you need to listen to him every time you start a new game? Well, [b]soon you’ll be able to politely tell him that you’ve heard everything[/b] he has to say already – [b]skipping his dialogues and the entire 1st day altogether[/b]. Which should make restarting the story less tedious.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/f9aefc618101583601bc64daef4cacc2ecacefb0.gif[/img]

Before you ask: we did consider making a skip button, which would unlock after the first walkthrough. However, the way dialogues work now, we’d have to manually add it to every single dialogue in the game. Which is not a small task. And also, you might accidentally skip important info when speaking to other guests. 

On that note, [b]we’d like to adjust the logic for the FEMA agent as well[/b]. Right now, he prioritizes taking away the guests who you’ve checked for Visitor signs, but didn’t threaten with the shotgun. And since it tends to happen with the characters you’re invested in learning more about – you might potentially miss out on seeing their story through the end.

[h3]Most importantly, all of this is going to be [b]available… Today![/b][/h3]
Not Tomorrow. Today!
https://steamcommunity.com/games/3180070/announcements/detail/498332997840274638?snr=2___

Lastly, let’s talk about something that's going to take us a bit longer to implement – [b]additional languages[/b]. It’s hard to hide anything happening with a game’s page nowadays, but, honestly, we weren’t even thinking about it. The reason why the release version was localized into fewer languages is that translating games takes up a lot of time and resources. And we simply didn’t have them before. 

So, we would like to honour what we’ve promised and introduce the following languages in the upcoming months:
[list]
[*] Ukrainian
[*] Polish
[*] Turkish
[*] Italian
[/list]
We’ll try to deliver them all at once, but, [b]depending on how long the translation itself takes, they might be added in separate updates[/b]. Hopefully, they will be here before you decide to replay the game once more.

In any case, [b]No, I’m not a Human has already passed 100,000 copies sold![/b] And we’d like to extend [b]a heartfelt thanks to all of you[/b]. For playing. For supporting us. For discussing the game. And for giving it so much praise. You probably hear this a lot, but [b]it does mean a world to us[/b]. And we would like to give back, and add [b]even more features to No, I’m not a Human in the future![/b]

For now, though, that’s all we have to share. Oh, wait, actually, there is [b]one more tiny thing[/b]. We have a [b]tie-in game bot on both Trioskaz and CR Channel Discords[/b]. It’s not a big thing per se, but might be a fun little daily ritual for you. So join either server (or both) and [b]look for the Freak Collector category![/b]

Alright, see ya on the other side!

[i]Trioskaz & CRITICAL REFLEX[/i]

notes.title: No, I’m not a Human is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
The coveted day we’ve all been waiting for has finally come. [b]No, I’m not a Human is available to buy, play, dread and contemplate over.[/b] Step into the anxiety-ridden world on a brink of apocalypse – and be the witness to its final breath.

[previewyoutube=IBftyLgNjyU;full][/previewyoutube]

What’s on offer? Glad you’ve asked:
[list]
[*] [b]Dozens upon dozens of guests[/b] – repulsive, broken, cunning, lonely, hopeful, alluring… yet human?
[*] [b]Multiple endings[/b] – things will end either way, but how? That depends entirely on your decisions;
[*] Gadgets, tools, consumables – you’re going to need all and any help to get through the end days;
[*] [b]Slew of achievements[/b] – some celebrate the simple things, while the others provide substantial challenge for your playthrough;
[*] [b]Plenty of secrets[/b] – not everything is revealed, nor are you on rails. To uncover everything, keep your brain on, and your eyes open.
[/list]
But, seriously, you should just go and play the game! Especially since it’s on a 10% discount for the next couple weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/e346098b5229dde4835d5829d97fa15760c2edb1.gif[/img]

From the outside, the final release of No, I’m not a Human probably didn’t take too long. But to us it felt like eternity. And [b]we’re so grateful for all the support you’ve shown to the game[/b] before it even came out.
Have fun (or rather fun dread)!

UPD: and if you've encountered a bug — please, share it on Steam Discussions!

notes.title: Release Date Reveal and New Trailer
notes.content:
[p]Heed the preach and spread the word: [b]No, I’m not a Human is coming out on September 15th[/b]. Anticipation, anxiety, pride, and so many more emotions fill us as we approach the date. But it’s inevitable, like Death itself. 

Don’t go telling your friends just yet, though. First, watch the announcement trailer.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube=2k64-X_zNGg;full][/previewyoutube][p][b][/b][/p][p][/p][p]Here’s who, and what to expect on September 15th:[/p][list][*][p]Several dozens of guests – with unique and troubled personalities, and equally hagridden looks;[/p][/*][*][p]Multiple endings – waiting for the Apocalypse doesn’t mean you know when and how your own story ends;[/p][/*][*][p]Many more things to help you survive the scheming Visitors – we hope you like smoking and drinking kombucha;[/p][/*][*][p]Secrets, secrets, secrets – unexpected resolutions to your guests’ stories, hidden rooms, mysterious achievements, and wild things happening outside the window.[/p][/*][/list][p]At this point we’ve spoiled pretty much all we’d like to spoil before release. The game has so many more new guests, events and features – and all of them will carry a much bigger impact if we keep them a secret.  
[/p][p]And if you were wondering, how the early experience compares to the demo – just know that energy management plays a much bigger role now.
[/p][p][img src="https://i.postimg.cc/FzCq0rCf/Cucumber.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]The wait is almost over.[/i][/p][p]
[/p][p]Looking for more delightfully dreadful games? Take a look at Eclipsium — a mind-and-heart-bending horror exploration game, where the environment bends and flows like a faulty memory. But, desperate to recover even a sliver of what’s dear, you delve into this mad world ever deeper.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2419670/Eclipsium/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]And Carimara: Beneath the forlorn limbs is creepy whimsy about asking the right questions to the weird inhabitants of its grove. Are you willing to lay your head in order to realise someone else’s wish?[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3570370/CARIMARA_Beneath_the_forlorn_limbs/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]This time we’re signing off with a question. Do vultures consume only the deceased? And when the end is all but assured for everyone – does it turn the entire World into a macabre banquet? [/p][p][/p][p][i]Trioskaz & Critical Reflex[/i][/p][p]

notes.title: SNF Demo Patch
notes.content:
[p]Heya! 

[b]Thank you for playing the demo! And for finding and reporting a bunch of bugs — which we have now fixed[/b]. Some of those were… pretty [i]unorthodox[/i], like pulling a guest from their room just to shoot them in another one. But anyway, here are the patch notes, so you can enjoy the demo (and eventually the full game) without these annoyances![/p][p][/p][h2]Patch Notes[/h2][p][/p][h3]Changes:[/h3][list][*][p]Changed the Super Visitor’s smile in one of his sprites;[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Changed the photo of a desktop near the phone to instead feature the photo of the Owner’s wife.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Fixes:[/h3][list][*][p][b]On first launch, the demo turns on the Vsync by default, and sets display resolution as close to 1080p as possible,[/b] after accounting for your display’s dimensions (1920x1080 for 16:9, 1728x1090 for 16:10 and etc.). [i]On any subsequent launches, the demo will still save any custom settings you might set.[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the issues with [b]“Who You Gonna Call?”[/b], [b]“Family Dinner”[/b] and [b]“Harsh Compromise”[/b] achievements; [/p][/*][*][p][b]You can no longer drink all the beer during item-use animation[/b]. Sorry, but turns out excessive drinking really is not good for you;[/p][/*][*][p][b]The game no longer softlocks if you get a visit from the FEMA agent[/b], while you have nobody else at your house. He’s just a human after all…[/p][/*][*][p][b]You can no longer “pull out” a guest from their room[/b] by quitting it while initiating the dialogue. As such, it’s also [b]not possible to execute them in another room and get softlocked[/b] when returning to the guest’s original room;[/p][/*][*][p][b]The fridge and other similar interactables no longer become non-interactable[/b] if you spam Exit while opening the fridge;[/p][/*][*][p][b]The game no longer reads the first click on the window as a proper input[/b], when bringing it back from being out-of-focus;[/p][/*][*][p][b]Initial fix for the cursor appearing in 3D parts of the game[/b] and blocking you from interactions. We’ve found one potential scenario of this happening, but couldn’t get it show up otherwise. So if you encounter it still — let us know.[/p][/*][/list][p]
Enjoy the demo and Steam Next Fest! And don’t forget to share your feedback with us. Cheers![/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: The Updated Demo is Here!
notes.content:
[p]New features, new guests, and new experience for multiple runs — The Steam Next Fest Demo is available NOW![/p][p][/p][p]But first, [i]how about a new trailer as well?[/i][/p][previewyoutube="AQT92TOri-I;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Now, let’s get into what you can expect from the updated demo. The guests are waiting.[/p][p]We’d like to highlight one[b] specific feature in this version[/b] first. Because, in our opinion, it adds quite a bit [b]more uncertainty and anxiety to your playthroughs[/b]. And that feature is [b]randomization[/b].[/p][p][/p][img src="https://i.postimg.cc/brhqqLfT/Post-Random.gif"][/img]

[p][b]Now[/b] [b]some of the guests will have their true identity and the day of their appearance randomized on each run[/b]. Of course, the most important characters like the Neighbour, the Prophet, the Super Impostor and FEMA soldier still have set parameters and will show up exactly as before. But everyone else? Well, you’d better be careful around them every time.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s not everything, though! Here’s the list of other notable features:[/p][list][*][p][b]Interactive radio[/b] — each day you’ll have the opportunity to hear a new broadcast. You’ll have to catch the right frequency to hear it clearly though;[/p][/*][*][p][b]More stuff on the TV[/b] — after you’ve watched the morning broadcast, you can tune in for more shows during the day. Maybe something important might pop up there as well, who knows;[/p][/*][*][p][b]New characters[/b] — will you risk your safety and let them in, or let them burn in the raging Sun?[/p][/*][*][p][b]Extended backstories for each character[/b] — more personality for the guests and more weight to your decisions. Be sure talk to them… or don’t, if you want your conscience to stay clean;[/p][/*][*][p][b]Consumables[/b] — true “bachelor fridge” experience, complete with beer and energy drinks. More of them will be featured in the full game;[/p][/*][*][p][b]Achievements [/b]— a small selection of feats for you to conquer and some spice for your experience with the demo;[/p][/*][*][p][b]And more[/b] — updated dialogues and text, upgraded UI, new sounds, bunch of small fixes and improvements![/p][/*][/list][p][b]One last thing[/b], but arguably even more important than the new features. After you’ve played the updated demo — [b]be sure to fill out the feedback form[/b] presented to you after you close the game. [b]We would really value your opinion[/b] on the new features, as well as your overall impressions of the demo![/p][p][/p][p]And in case you miss the feedback form, here’s a direct link:[/p][p][url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdmAgMji5zSCzKOeXKCvh7-Lcye2DBmLzZfzZO2rMZa-jrCRA/viewform" style="button"]No, I'm not a Human Feedback Form[/url][/p][p][/p][p]You might want to [b]join CR Channel Discord[/b] as well to discuss your impressions with other players. Especially since we a have [b]couple cool No, I’m Not a Human activities in the works[/b] for you to participate in while you wait for the full release![/p][p][/p][p]Speaking of: [b]we have a silly little activity going on over at Twitter\\X[/b], where each week the community suggests what we should put into a glass jar to later preserve. Who knows, maybe if all goes well with the jar, it might even appear in-game?
[/p][p]And if you’re a fan of our studio, absolutely [b]join Trioskaz Official Discord[/b] server. We sometimes host [b]chaotic Q&As there, share news and insights[/b] before anywhere else, and just like to chat with our community members.

By the way, our studio is going to release another game soon — [b]Lost in the Roots[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2872240/Lost_in_the_Roots/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]It's a [b]2D adventure with a tangled story about guilt, in which a girl is kidnapped[/b] and held captive in some unknown attic located somewhere inside a giant living Forst in the countryside. Who and why has taken the girl to such godforsaken place? And what do you do when you have nowhere to run? [/p][p][/p][p]That’s everything… for now at least. Enjoy the updated demo, and don’t forget to let us know your thoughts on it![/p][p]
[i]“A man would rise from the dead and speak. And people won’t believe him”[/i][/p][p]Trioskaz & Critical Reflex.[/p][p]

notes.title: Devlog: A Brief Foray into the Horrors
notes.content:
Many games are built on fears, but how diverse are they—and how deeply do they shape the very essence of gameplay? It's not just eerie visuals, screamers, or unsettling sounds. Today, we want to show you how internal contradictions can influence your decisions and evoke a genuine fear of consequences. It’s much deeper than it appears at first glance.

[h2]No, I'm not a Human: When Trust Becomes a Luxury[/h2]

[h3]Example 1: "What are you even afraid of?!"[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/7f6ed473997eae2890c9d903f5dfb01e3b0efeb9.png[/img]

Imagine this scenario: a tall guy from the bar approaches your door. He’s clearly skeptical—mocking, even—of the Guest signs you’re trying to check in order to decide whether he’s trustworthy. His absurd yet oddly perceptive comments make you question: do these rules even work?

But the more he denies any danger, the stronger your anxiety grows. This is a classic case where denying fear only amplifies it. As a player, you start to wonder: was this man really a Guest? Or is it just your paranoia? In moments like these, the game plunges you into a whirlpool of doubt, where every choice could be fatal.


[h3]Example 2: "A Friend’s Daughter or a Threat?"[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/1ffbf47c2a13f8fa8e100e4dace921aaaab5c6ac.png[/img]

One of the most morally ambiguous scenes occurs when the neighbor’s daughter—the child of a friend who was recently murdered—knocks on your door. You know the rules of the game and understand the weight of responsibility behind each decision. Letting her in means risking the lives of those already inside. Leaving her outside might condemn the daughter of someone you knew and respected to death.

This situation brings to the surface one of the main fears explored in the game: the fear of making the wrong choice. What if you make the wrong decision? What if the cost of that mistake is too high? Will you still be the same person after making a harsh—but possibly correct—choice?

This dilemma forces players to deeply reflect on what it means to be human in a world where trust has become a luxury. But sometimes fears aren’t just internal—they take physical form as well.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/b2b2dbd85d5dbd62a05104068fd1a779a7a65e13.gif[/img]

In Lost in the Roots , for example, one of the most unforgettable moments awaits you: an encounter with a monstrous entity symbolizing the womb. This figure embodies all the fears associated with growing up: responsibility, loss of innocence, and the realization that the world is no longer as simple as it seemed in childhood. For the protagonist, this monster becomes a metaphor for her inner struggle. She realizes that every step she takes alters the future.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2872240/Lost_in_the_Roots/

And this is just a glimpse of the horrors you’ll face in our games. Are you ready?

notes.title: New Trailer and Updated Demo Details
notes.content:
We’re back, with more news about No, I’m not a Human. The newest trailer, choke full of disturbingly exciting teasers. Juicy details about the inevitable Steam Next Fest demo. All the good stuff.

Let’s not waste any time and get into it — after all, what if the Sun explodes tomorrow?!

[previewyoutube=7bFciBjEuOk;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]“Would you like to know more?”[/i]

We could spend quite some time explaining things in the trailer, but it would be much more impactful if you could experience everything firsthand. After all, you won’t be waiting for too long — [b]No, I’m Not a Human is releasing this Fall[/b]!

And before that, you’ll get a chance to experience an updated demo as well. [b]Summer is approaching — and with it comes Steam Next Fest[/b]. Since we were hard at work expanding and improving the game, it’s only natural to release an [b]updated demo[/b] for it. 

But what exactly will be waiting at the doorstep when you boot up the demo? Or rather… who? Let’s address the last part first.

[h3]New Guests[/h3]

Be prepared for a visit from around a [b]dozen of guests — both returning faces and new ones.[/b] This time, [b]many of them will have their identities and first visits randomized[/b]. This means that, while some characters will have a fixed identity and appear on certain days, the rest are going to remain a mystery every playthrough. Here are [i]some[/i] of the new guests.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/8933a33ed825f770a15bbdde428e0d83ad4c18fd.png[/img]
Like Yin and Yang with a drop of each other inside of them, they each process the End Days in their own, conflicting ways. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/ee2f9fb48640f4e93aa614753d9b9424f16acd68.png[/img]
Already one foot in the grave, this disfigured man is still clinging to life, gnawing at it with a maw of regrets.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/b5885c20f4ac450e32d161839619316f51fded75.png[/img]
His life was Hell even before the events, but he has a rather… [i]positive[/i] outlook on everything. Human or not, it’s hard to distinguish his lies from truths even on the best of days.

And, of course, we’re including an additional clue for finding out who’s who. What? No, it’s not a weird one — your life depends on it! Come on.

[h3]New Activities[/h3]

While we don’t want to spoil all of the stuff by putting it in the demo — we’ve still added a number of actions you can perform each day. Just keep in mind, that most of them require energy, so try to be strategic about using them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/e3a40c075180a8e68e8f2e9a618794ba58cb94d5.png[/img]
“Video killed the radio star” — well, not in this game. Pick up that radio and meticulously scrub the FM wastelands with a channel selector. Maybe you’ll even hear some good news for a change!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/3e9eb98cb39abafb20e64594c7740b5f9eb27fe8.gif[/img]
Overwhelmed by certain feelings for one of your guests, but can’t express them directly? Just use the postcard to do it anonymously. Write their name and give it to the good people at FEMA. The rest will sort itself out, don’t worry! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/e0d6259fd6b0330ea119f1177428c9403983f88f.gif[/img]
Some days are just more exhausting than others. And to help you get through them, your fridge will contain the best caffeinated energy drink around. Well, one of the best from the few that are left anyways. Just don’t get addicted to it — there is nobody to deliver you more, [i]yet[/i].

No, I’m Not a Human demo will take you through 4 to 5 in-game days. And there is plenty to experience in that time. Oh, almost forgot: sometimes the Visitors might not pass away as peacefully when you execute them. 

By the way, our studio is going to release another game soon — [b]Lost in the Roots[/b].

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2872240/Lost_in_the_Roots/

It's a 2D adventure with a tangled story about guilt, in which a girl is kidnapped and held captive in some unknown attic located somewhere inside a giant living Forst in the countryside. Who and why has taken the girl to such godforsaken place? And what do you do when you have nowhere to run? 

That’s all the news for today, everyone! Stay tuned for more info down the road, and, of course, the demo release of No, I’m Not a Human. 

[i]“A man would rise from the dead and speak. And people won’t believe him”[/i]
Trioskaz & Critical Reflex.

notes.title: Publishing Deal and the Road Ahead
notes.content:
Firstly, most of us appreciate visual content. So here’s a brand new trailer for No, I am Not a Human to put you into the right mood!

[previewyoutube=kIah1uiawBY;full][/previewyoutube]

But let’s do a [b]quick rundown of what No, I am Not a Human is[/b]  — for those who might’ve joined us just recently. 

[b]No, I am Not a Human is, no other way to put it, an anxiety horror.[/b] It’s full of paranoia and distrust — raising the question of how much humanity can be preserved in a face of fear of death, and what exactly awaits us after.   

[b]You will play as a citizen under a lockdown, caused by extreme Sun activity during the day and mysterious cryptids — known only as the Visitors, — roaming the night.[/b] Since “strength is numbers” you’ll need people at your house. But you can never know if they’re human themselves, since the Visitors are quite adapt at mimicking them. And it’s only up to you to make the toughest decision: would you rather survive at all costs, or try to also preserve your humanity through all of this? 

On that note, [b]we’ve got a publishing deal with Critical Reflex[/b], who have provided us with much needed security. You might know them best as the people who brought [b]Buckshot Roulette[/b] over to Steam and helped [b]Mouthwashing [/b]reach new heights. 

Having a publisher means that [b]we can afford to do more[/b] for No, I am Not a Human. Like localizing the game into additional languages. For example:
[list]
[*] Chinese
[*] French
[*] German
[*] Japanese
[*] Korean
[*] Portuguese
[*] Brazilian Portuguese
[*] Spanish
[*] LATAM Spanish
[/list]
[i]Do note, that this list might change before release, but this is what we’re planning to do.[/i]

Also, we can dedicate more resources to [b]polishing and testing the game[/b]. And it’s going to have [b]quite a number of content permutations![/b] So we can definitely use some extra hands looking at all the variations. For release, we plan to add:
[list]
[*] [b]More clues for the Visitors[/b] — to keep you on your toes and excited to do another voyeuristic check of your guests, our lead artist has drawn more teeth, nails and eyes for the game.
[*] [b]Include more of the Visitors themselves[/b] — our aim is to make each playthrough feel fresh. And to help with this, we are going to expand the cast of Visitors, allowing you to encounter only a select few of them each run. 
[*] [b]Add multiple endings[/b] — Fully drawn, not just a text epilogue! Some of them will be more obvious than others. All of them are going to depend on your actions and choices.
[*] [b]Consumables[/b] — drink some kombucha to brighten your day. Or a “can of liquid courage”, commonly known as “the beer”.
[*] [b]Interactable telephone[/b] — your lifeline for boredom, starvation and  informational collapse. Not all of the numbers are going to be in a phone book though.
[*] [b]A cat?![/b] — yes! And you’ll appreciate the soothing company of its goofy-looking face, trust us.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183347/327387d44c2978a963c7ca49894fcab640221182.gif[/img]

We hope that you’re as excited to delve into No, I am Not a Human, as we are excited about releasing it! [b]More information about the game, developer diaries and teasers will drop during the upcoming months.[/b] So stay tuned!

[i]“A man would rise from the dead and speak. And people won’t believe him”[/i]
Trioskaz & Critical Reflex.

notes.title: The game from one of the developers of No I'm Not Human is releasing 12.05!
notes.content:
We want to shine a light on an upcoming indie horror game from one of our devs and our talented friends at [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/SUPERBOBERBROS]Bober Bros[/url]!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3037930/Bober_Bros_The_Hole/][b]The Hole[/b][/url] is a raw, deeply personal exploration of family abuse and human horror — more intimate and visceral than our own. It doesn’t rely on cheap scares but instead captures the suffocating tension of a broken home, a chilling narrative grounded in real-life experiences.

Their work left a lasting impression on us. it’s honest, unsettling, and unforgettable. If you’ve been drawn into the atmosphere and social themes of our own game, you’ll find even darker truths in The Hole.

And keep an eye out — you might spot a familiar character in their world. 😉

Support this courageous storytelling by [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3037930/Bober_Bros_The_Hole/]wishlisting The Hole[/url] today.
